raw_response:
I am old now, and with only 4.1 mu I cannot gamble. I do what has worked on my land and what people around me do. Wheat and maize together keep the land busy and keep some grain coming in. The money is tight because some family members work outside and are not always home, so I will not chase fancy things. I will use the well when the crop really needs water, but I will not pump too many times because electricity and water cost money. Fertilizer, I would rather not cut too much. If I save a little on fertilizer and the crop turns thin, that loss is bigger than the money saved.

For wheat, I will sow in early October, not too late, after the maize comes off. I usually put some fertilizer under before sowing, then watch the wheat after winter. If the leaves are light and the stand looks weak around jointing, I topdress again. I do not count things like a technician, but I know roughly how much my field can carry. Wheat here usually wants a few waterings, so I plan for three if the season is normal. For maize, the time is short after wheat harvest, so I will not do heavy tillage. I will clear the field quickly, make it neat, and sow right away. Maize grows fast in summer, so I give it one base dressing and one more when it is getting tall. If rain is enough, I save the pumping money; if it stays dry at tasseling, I will irrigate once. I expect an ordinary year, not a bumper year.
